Hello Andrew,

Thank you for your comment.

By describing the configuration in EM we're trying to locate the physical device. Maybe Bus, Port, Configuration and Interface might be more helpful here? The kernel will automatically create an interface when it sees the MCTP interface descriptor. The interface can be located by looking under the net/ subdirectory:

```
# ls -1d /sys/bus/usb/devices/1-1/1-1:1.0/net/*
/sys/bus/usb/devices/1-1/1-1:1.0/net/mctpusb0
```

This is essentially:

```
/sys/bus/usb/devices/${Bus}-${Port}/${Bus}-${Port}:${Configuration}-${Interface}/net/...
```

Interface name assigned to USB devices from kernel is indeterministic in nature i.e for x-y.z bus-port.path, it's not necessary that mctpusbX would always be assigned since its completely based on first come first serve basis for usb devices.

for eg : if we have two USB devices as 1-1 and 1-2 path, and we attach first USB device (1-1) and later the second one (1-2), interface names may get assigned as mctpusb0 and mctpusb1 for first and second device respectively. Since USB is hot pluggable in nature, we can detach and reattach devices and this time if in reverse sequence i.e second device followed by first, then interface name for second device would end up as mctpusb0 while for the first usb device as mctpusb1.

 
Right now we don't have a proper mechanism in upstream to map the USB device's bus-port.path to its right interface name.

I agree at kernel sysfs path this data will exist but this too would be indeterministic, thus exposing BUS, PORT, CONFIGURATION etc for usb device on EM configuration might not be directly feasible.

Besides this patch aims to handle dynamic EID assignment to the mctp usb devices which as in whole doesn't necessarily requires such data from MCTP Reactor end.

But I completely agree with you to expose these details of devices once we are looking into integrating Static EID assignment to the USB endpoints.

> Interface name assigned to USB devices from kernel is indeterministic in nature i.e for x-y.z bus-port.path, it's not necessary that mctpusbX would always be assigned since its completely based on first come first serve basis for usb devices.

Yes, this is why it's not appropriate to specify the interface name in an EM schema IMO.

> Right now we don't have a proper mechanism in upstream to map the USB device's bus-port.path to its right interface name.

I gave you one above. Use the bus, port, config and interface values to locate the device in sysfs, then look at the directory name under `net/`. From there you just need to take the basename. Expanding on my example above:

```
# basename /sys/bus/usb/devices/1-1/1-1:1.0/net/*
mctpusb0
```

> I agree at kernel sysfs path this data will exist but this too would be indeterministic

One concern here is a stable alias for the bus, but beyond that the port topology is stable.

> Besides this patch aims to handle dynamic EID assignment to the mctp usb devices which as in whole doesn't necessarily requires such data from MCTP Reactor end.

If that's the case, why are you proposing an EM schema (I'm the author of `mctpreactor`)? We can have mctpreactor respond to udev or netlink events to automatically set up the endpoint dynamically.

> > Interface name assigned to USB devices from kernel is indeterministic in nature i.e for x-y.z bus-port.path, it's not necessary that mctpusbX would always be assigned since its completely based on first come first serve basis for usb devices.
> 
> Yes, this is why it's not appropriate to specify the interface name in an EM schema IMO.
> 
> > Right now we don't have a proper mechanism in upstream to map the USB device's bus-port.path to its right interface name.
> 
> I gave you one above. Use the bus, port, config and interface values to locate the device in sysfs, then look at the directory name under `net/`. From there you just need to take the basename. Expanding on my example above:
> 
> ```
> # basename /sys/bus/usb/devices/1-1/1-1:1.0/net/*
> mctpusb0
> ```
> 
> > I agree at kernel sysfs path this data will exist but this too would be indeterministic
> 
> One concern here is a stable alias for the bus, but beyond that the port topology is stable.
>

Would it be best that we let something external do that? Something like a udev rule that sets  an altname to the net i/f via a udev rule, (via something like: `ip link property add dev $env{INTERFACE} altname mctpusb<bus_id>-<port_path>-<cfg>-<intf>`

The EM config can continue to use the alt interface name rather than having to piece that together from sysfs.

> > Besides this patch aims to handle dynamic EID assignment to the mctp usb devices which as in whole doesn't necessarily requires such data from MCTP Reactor end.
> 
> If that's the case, why are you proposing an EM schema (I'm the author of `mctpreactor`)? We can have mctpreactor respond to udev or netlink events to automatically set up the endpoint dynamically.

We need an EM schema for 1) creating the association between the MCTP endpoint objects and the config and 2) the aim is still to get to static endpoints in the future.

> Would it be best that we let something external do that? Something like a udev rule that sets an altname to the net i/f via a udev rule, (via something like: ip link property add dev $env{INTERFACE} altname mctpusb<bus_id>-<port_path>-<cfg>-<intf>

I feel that's moving the problem rather than removing it. Now you need to coordinate the custom udev rule with the EM configuration, and you still end up needing to know the details anyway with the scheme you've proposed.

EM configs are about describing hardware and their relationships. I don't see any reason not to continue that by describing Bus/Port/Configuration/Interface for USB devices directly.

> We need an EM schema for 1) creating the association between the MCTP endpoint objects and the config and 2) the aim is still to get to static endpoints in the future.

Understood, however, EM configs that lack any hardware context are detached in a way that makes them a bit meaningless. However, with the scheme discussed above we can fix that.

> I feel that's moving the problem rather than removing it. Now you need to coordinate the custom udev rule with the EM configuration, and you still end up needing to know the details anyway with the scheme you've proposed.
> 
> EM configs are about describing hardware and their relationships. I don't see any reason not to continue that by describing Bus/Port/Configuration/Interface for USB devices directly.
>

OK, that is fair. We can update this config to include that information and make the corresponding reactor changes to consume that info, get the right interface name from sysfs and proceed to use that to call into mctpd. Once that is done, would this and the corresponding Reactor change be good to go?

> > We need an EM schema for 1) creating the association between the MCTP endpoint objects and the config and 2) the aim is still to get to static endpoints in the future.
>

IMO yes, but I'm not an EM maintainer, so you'll need to convince them too 😊

FWIW note the implementation for resolving the interface name of `MCTPI2CTarget`s:

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/plugins/gitiles/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/02c4366be0eb2409c81784c989dfb690cd41af58/src/mctp/MCTPEndpoint.cpp#397

@andrew@codeconstruct.com.au, this is the new EM schema which takes in the RootHubPath like `"/sys/devices/platform/ahb/1e6a3000.usb"` and deduces the deterministic busnum attribute in the reactor. 
Example EM schema would look like
```
"Exposes": [
        {
	     "RootHubPath": "/sys/devices/platform/ahb/1e6a3000.usb",
    	     "Port": "1.2.5",
             "Configuration": "1",
             "InterfaceNum": “0”,
	      "Name": "mctpusb_x”,
         "Type": "MCTPUSBDevice"
        }
    ]
```
Reactor Changes for your reference: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/80452

@andrew@codeconstruct.com.au any furthe comments here? I've added a topic to all the related patches that I'm testing on an upstream Nvidia platform - https://gerrit.openbmc.org/q/topic:%22mctp-usb-config%22 .
Resolving this based on the above comment.

Acknowledged, added one example EM schema in the 'tested' section of the commit msg also.

This isn't just one port though - your defining a topology here. I think we have a few things to resolve here:

- Should this be 1 port or many?
- If many perhaps we should use a list of integers rather than a string

Yes, the wording and the name here should be updated. Perhaps `PortNumbers` is more appropriate. I am kind of on the fence about the actual data type, though. Not sure what we gain by making this an int array only to later convert it to the format necessary to translate it for sysfs.

Is it common for hardware schematics to use the dot notation? If so, maybe it's fine, but I suspect that representation is Linux-specific (even if it's somewhat intuitive). It's the job of `mctpreactor` to assemble the provided information into something that's useful in the context of the software implementation (interacting with Linux).

> Is it common for hardware schematics to use the dot notation?

No, the HW schematics/diagrams I have seen mostly just show individual hub connections and port numbers (and the root port is often left out because it is typically 1)

> It's the job of mctpreactor to assemble the provided information into something that's useful in the context of the software implementation (interacting with Linux).

True, but then the Root hub devpath is already something linux specific. As such I don't see an issue with bleeding some Linux specific detail into EM configs which are meant for a Linux based OpenBMC distribution, no?

> but then the Root hub devpath is already something linux specific.

I'm not enamoured with `RootHubPath` for that reason, which was why I was suggesting a deterministic bus index. I2C busses achieve this with aliases in the devicetree, the same might be done here (and we use `Bus` instead of `RootHubPath`).

It's probably time to find an EM maintainer to weigh in 😊

Hey @andrew@codeconstruct.com.au, so adding the aliases in dt like 
```
        usb10 = &ehci0;
        usb20 = &ehci1;
        usb30 = &uhci;
```
exposes them in `/proc/device-tree/aliases` and not in `/sys/bus/usb/devices` which still shows a usb1 instead of usb10, 

So what I am thinking is reading the of_node property and mapping it against the device-tree alias, would that be an acceptable solution? Please feel free to point me to any other approaches which might be less cumbersome. 😊
```root@gb200nvl-hmc:/sys/bus/usb/devices/usb1# readlink -f of_node
/sys/firmware/devicetree/base/ahb/usb@1e6a1000
```

I don’t know how we make this usable without some extra code in entity manager similar to what we’re doing for relative i2c busses. If you take the GB300 card as an example, you might have some USB endpoint via MCTP. That card can be plugged into a server from Meta or a server from Google, and there can be multiple of those cards. One of us could use multiple root ports off the BMC in our design and the other could use a USB hub. You can’t express this by putting a static MCTP-USB device into the GB300 EM config as you’ve proposed it here.

> I don’t know how we make this usable without some extra code in entity manager similar to what we’re doing for relative i2c busses

As it stands its only usable in the configuration for the board containing the BMC from where we can describe the absolute topology (where while the device is USB-attached and USB supports hot-plug, the topology is fixed in the hardware design). You're right that it's not yet useful for pluggable cards.

The extra code we need in EM is probably best hashed out in a design doc. Having thought about it a bit, I suspect it might be useful for EM to process events from a `NETLINK_KOBJECT_UEVENT` socket. Other choices seem unwieldy (e.g. leaving that to udev, and then poking EM via a D-Bus interface from a helper binary launched from a udev rule like we do for phosphor-led-sysfs).

USB is self-describing so I think it's reasonable that we allow probes based on the info there and not tie it to a FRU EEPROM? This will get us inventory for the device in EM (which is necessary for the purpose of OpenBMC and eliminates a udev-only solution). From there we can fill in bus and port info from sysfs based on the uevent.

> So what I am thinking is reading the of_node property and mapping it against the device-tree alias, would that be an acceptable solution?

It would be better if the usb subsystem applied aliases itself like the i2c subsystem. Can you send a patch upstream?

I'm looking at the above, and I don't see how this could work.  Could you include an example of

BMC -> Mainboard(Embedded usb hub) -> USB MCU device

The full layout for those three components?  The way you're describing 1.2.5 makes it seem like you're putting the whole topology in a single component, but remember that 1.2.5 in the above example would be

BMC(USB port 1) -> Mainboard (Hub port 2) -> USB device (Device 5) 

So that config needs split across 3 config files, similar to what patrick has pointed out.

This could work if the USB topology is contained in the same entity or we're able to identify a platform (by combining lookup of multiple entities; see next commit). I could test this on an upstream nvidia pltform - see https://gerrit.openbmc.org/q/topic:%22mctp-usb-config%22

This is not the Linux/MCTP definition of "Interface" but rather the USB device definition, e.g. from `9.2.3 Configuration` of `usb_20.pdf`:

> 9.2.3 Configuration
>...
> Within a single configuration, a device may support multiple interfaces. An interface is a related set of endpoints that present a single feature or function of the device to the host. The protocol used to communicate with this related set of endpoints and the purpose of each endpoint within the interface may be specified as part of a device class or vendor-specific definition.
